proposals.before: In the twenty-third year of the reign (1843), serving as a reviser he presided over the Sichuan provincial examinations, was later made reader-in-waiting, and rose in succession to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, with concurrent charge of the Ministry of War.
proposals.after: In the twenty-third year of the reign (1843), serving as a Hanlin investigating editor (jian tao) he presided over the Sichuan provincial examinations, was later made reader-in-waiting, and rose in succession to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, with concurrent charge of the Ministry of War.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is Academician/Bachelor of the Grand Secretariat, not Grand Secretary (大學士); 檢討 is a Hanlin compiling/investigating post, not a generic 'reviser'.

proposals.before: At first Guofan meant to petition for permission to observe the full three-year mourning. Guo Songsong said, "You have long aspired to set the realm to rights—if you do not seize this moment to serve, what becomes of your duty to sovereign and father?

proposals.reason: 郭嵩燾 is Guo Songtao, not Guo Songsong.

decisions.after: In the twenty-third year of the reign (1843), while serving as an Investigating Editor in the Hanlin Academy, he presided over the Sichuan provincial examinations. He was later made Reader-in-Waiting and rose in succession to Academician of the Grand Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites, while concurrently overseeing the Ministry of War.
decisions.reason: The source distinguishes 檢討, a Hanlin post, from 內閣學士, an Academician of the Grand Secretariat; the original wrongly promoted the latter to Grand Secretary. The revised wording keeps the proposal's correction while replacing parenthetical split pinyin with natural English and clarifying the sequence of offices.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以檢討典試四川，再轉侍讀，累遷內閣學士

decisions.reason: The focus unit explicitly names 郭嵩燾, whose name is Guo Songtao. 'Guo Songsong' is an unsupported mistranscription.
The same 郭嵩燾 occurrence controls the literal field; Songtao is the person's established reading, while Songsong has no support in the Chinese.
The abbreviated 嵩燾 refers back to Guo Songtao, so the proposed correction removes a repeated false name while preserving the sentence's meaning.
